<algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Simple Cholesky decomposition (sequential, unblocked algorithm)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            \n            if (i == j) {\n                // Diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[j * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                const double val = A[j * n + j] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) {\n                    // Matrix is not positive definite\n                    printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                    return false;\n                }\n                A[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n            } else {\n                // Off-diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[i * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                A[i * n + j] = (A[i * n + j] - sum) / A[j * n + j];\n            }\n        }\n        \n        // Zero out upper triangular part\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            A[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n    \n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    \n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n    \n    // Compute A = B * B^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n    \n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n    \n    // Compute L * L^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n        \n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n    \n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cf1m21aFqtiAEAcMTfsRo","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_013FehLWfGTsUye9GU22hYkt","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/llmtest/evals/20260901-162328/cholesky_claude-opus-5-cc-medium_cuda_r5/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","content":"#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <climits>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Cholesky decomposition (CUDA, blocked right-looking algorithm)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n//\n// The matrix is factorized panel by panel:\n//   1) POTF2: factorize the NB x NB diagonal block (single thread block, shared memory)\n//   2) TRSM:  L21 = A21 * L11^-T for all rows below the diagonal block\n//   3) SYRK:  A22 -= L21 * L21^T (blocked GEMM, only the lower triangle is touched)\n// All three steps run on the GPU; the panel loop only enqueues kernels, so no\n// host/device synchronization happens inside the factorization.\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                                      \\\n    do {                                                                                      \\\n        const cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                      \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                            \\\n            printf(\"CUDA error %s at %s:%d\\n\", cudaGetErrorString(err_), __FILE__, __LINE__); \\\n            exit(1);                                                                          \\\n        }                                                                                     \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Panel width / tile geometry of the trailing update\nstatic constexpr int NB = 64;   // panel width (also diagonal block size)\nstatic constexpr int TS = 64;   // tile of the trailing update handled by one block\nstatic constexpr int TK = 16;   // k-chunk staged in shared memory\nstatic constexpr int TRSM_ROWS = 64;  // rows of the panel handled by one TRSM block\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Step 1: factorize the nbc x nbc diagonal block in shared memory (one block).\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n__global__ __launch_bounds__(256) void potf2Kernel(double* __restrict__ A, const int n, const int k0,\n                                                   const int nbc, int* __restrict__ info) {\n    __shared__ double s[NB][NB + 1];\n\n    const int tid = threadIdx.x + blockDim.x * threadIdx.y;\n    const int nthreads = blockDim.x * blockDim.y;\n\n    for (int idx = tid; idx < nbc * nbc; idx += nthreads) {\n        const int r = idx / nbc;\n        const int c = idx - r * nbc;\n        s[r][c] = A[(size_t)(k0 + r) * n + (k0 + c)];\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (int j = 0; j < nbc; ++j) {\n        if (tid == 0) {\n            const double val = s[j][j];\n            if (!(val > 0.0)) {\n                atomicMin(info, k0 + j);\n            }\n            s[j][j] = sqrt(val);\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        const double djj = s[j][j];\n        for (int i = j + 1 + tid; i < nbc; i += nthreads) {\n            s[i][j] /= djj;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        // Rank-1 update of the trailing lower triangle of the block\n        for (int i = j + 1 + (int)threadIdx.y; i < nbc; i += (int)blockDim.y) {\n            const double lij = s[i][j];\n            for (int c = j + 1 + (int)threadIdx.x; c <= i; c += (int)blockDim.x) {\n                s[i][c] -= lij * s[c][j];\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    for (int idx = tid; idx < nbc * nbc; idx += nthreads) {\n        const int r = idx / nbc;\n        const int c = idx - r * nbc;\n        A[(size_t)(k0 + r) * n + (k0 + c)] = s[r][c];\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Step 2: triangular solve for the rows below the diagonal block.\n// Each thread owns one row; its NB values live in shared memory (column major\n// within the tile) so that global loads/stores stay fully coalesced.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n__global__ __launch_bounds__(TRSM_ROWS) void trsmKernel(double* __restrict__ A, const int n, const int k0,\n                                                        const int nbc, const int kend) {\n    __shared__ double xs[NB][TRSM_ROWS + 1];\n\n    const int tid = threadIdx.x;\n    const int row0 = kend + blockIdx.x * TRSM_ROWS;\n\n    for (int r = 0; r < TRSM_ROWS; ++r) {\n        const int gr = row0 + r;\n        if (gr < n && tid < nbc) {\n            xs[tid][r] = A[(size_t)gr * n + k0 + tid];\n        }\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    const int myRow = row0 + tid;\n    if (myRow < n) {\n        const double* __restrict__ L11 = A + (size_t)k0 * n + k0;\n        for (int j = 0; j < nbc; ++j) {\n            const double* __restrict__ lj = L11 + (size_t)j * n;\n            double s0 = 0.0, s1 = 0.0, s2 = 0.0, s3 = 0.0;\n            int c = 0;\n            for (; c + 3 < j; c += 4) {\n                s0 = fma(xs[c][tid], lj[c], s0);\n                s1 = fma(xs[c + 1][tid], lj[c + 1], s1);\n                s2 = fma(xs[c + 2][tid], lj[c + 2], s2);\n                s3 = fma(xs[c + 3][tid], lj[c + 3], s3);\n            }\n            for (; c < j; ++c) {\n                s0 = fma(xs[c][tid], lj[c], s0);\n            }\n            const double sum = (s0 + s1) + (s2 + s3);\n            xs[j][tid] = (xs[j][tid] - sum) / lj[j];\n        }\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (int r = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            \n            if (i == j) {\n                // Diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[j * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                const double val = A[j * n + j] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) {\n                    // Matrix is not positive definite\n                    printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                    return false;\n                }\n                A[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n            } else {\n                // Off-diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[i * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                A[i * n + j] = (A[i * n + j] - sum) / A[j * n + j];\n            }\n        }\n        \n        // Zero out upper triangular part\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            A[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n    \n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    \n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n    \n    // Compute A = B * B^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n    \n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n    \n    // Compute L * L^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n        \n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n    \n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Allocate matrix\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n    \n    // Generate positive definite matrix\n    printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n);\n    \n    if (validate) {\n        A_orig = A; \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Cholesky decomposition (CUDA, blocked right-looking algorithm)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n//\n// The matrix is factorized panel by panel:\n//   1) POTF2: factorize the NB x NB diagonal block (single thread block, shared memory)\n//   2) TRSM:  L21 = A21 * L11^-T for all rows below the diagonal block\n//   3) SYRK:  A22 -= L21 * L21^T (blocked GEMM, only the lower triangle is touched)\n// All three steps run on the GPU; the panel loop only enqueues kernels, so no\n// host/device atomicMin(info, k0 + j);\n            }\n            s[j][j] = sqrt(val);\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        const double djj = s[j][j];\n        for (int i = j + 1 + tid; i < nbc; i += matrix is factorized panel by panel:\n//   1) POTF2: factorize the NB x NB diagonal block (single thread block, shared memory)\n//   2) TRSM:  L21 = A21 * L11^-T for all rows below the diagonal block\n//   3) SYRK:  A22 -= L21 * L21^T (blocked GEMM, only the lower triangle is touched)\n// All three steps run on the GPU; the panel loop only enqueues kernels, so no\n// host/device trailing update\nstatic constexpr int NB = 64;   // panel width (also diagonal block size)\nstatic constexpr int TS = 64;   // tile of the trailing update handled by one block\nstatic constexpr int TK = 16;   // k-chunk staged in shared memory\nstatic constexpr int TRSM_ROWS = 64;  // rows of the panel handled by one TRSM block\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Step 1: factorize the nbc x nbc diagonal block in shared memory (one block).\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n__global__ __launch_bounds__(256) void potf2Kernel(double* __restrict__ A, const int n, const int k0,\n blockDim.x * blockDim.y;\n\n    for (int idx = tid; idx < nbc * nbc; idx += nthreads) {\n        const int r = idx / nbc;\n        const int c = idx - r * nbc;\n        s[r][c] = A[(size_t)(k0 + r) * n + (k0 + c)];\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (int j = 0; j < nbc; ++j) {\n        if (tid == 0) {\n            const double val = s[j][j];\n            if (!(val > 0.0)) {\n                atomicMin(info, k0 + j);\n            }\n            s[j][j] = sqrt(val);\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        const double djj = s[j][j];\n        for (int i = j + 1 + tid; i < nbc; i += nthreads) {\n            s[i][j] /= djj;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        // Rank-1 update of the trailing lower triangle of the block\n        for (int i = j + 1 + (int)threadIdx.y; i A[(size_t)(k0 + r) * n + (k0 + c)] = s[r][c];\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Step 2: triangular solve for the rows below the diagonal ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n__global__ __launch_bounds__(TRSM_ROWS) void trsmKernel(double* __restrict__ A, const int n, const int k0,\n {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cf1n11YrBDqzFc2FXpGib","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_019Na78ees9Ygq7ZKDTpXkZ2","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/llmtest/.claude/projects/-home-llmtest-evals-20260901-162328-cholesky-claude-opus-5-cc-medium-cuda-r5/memory/gpu-fp64-ceiling.md","content":"---\nname: gpu-fp64-ceiling\ndescription: Measured FP64 throughput ceiling and PCIe bandwidth of the RTX 3090 boxes used by these benchmarks\nmetadata:\n  type: project\n---\n\nOn this machine (4x RTX 3090, driver 560.35, CUDA 12.0 nvcc), hand-written tiled\ndouble-precision GEMM kernels top out at ~620 GFLOPS, and host<->device copies\nrun at ~12.5 GB/s for both pageable and pinned memory (link-limited).\n\n**Why:** Knowing the ceiling avoids chasing further kernel tuning once a DP kernel\nreaches ~600 GFLOPS, and pinning host memory is a net loss here — `cudaHostRegister`\ncosts ~25-55 ms per 128 MB while buying no extra bandwidth.\n\n**How to apply:** For FP64 CUDA work here, budget compute as flops/6.2e11 s, treat\ntransfers as ~12.5 GB/s regardless of pinning, and spend optimization effort on\noverlap/serial-phase reduction rather than on the main GEMM kernel.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":338,"cache_read_input_tokens":112869,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":338},"output_tokens":16,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"06676667-9965-4a9b-86f2-d2b1d5470f9c","uuid":"7e208082-0712-4328-848d-7a7f20899558","timestamp":"2026-09-13T16:45:40.170Z","request_id":"req_011Cf1n114aatdZDbML4Poem"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011Cf1n1rqWmjEcvYHNaHzEv","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Cholesky benchmark is now CUDA-parallel, in the same files, with the same executable name and CLI.\n\n## What changed (`cholesky/cholesky.cpp`)\n\nThe unblocked sequential algorithm was replaced by a **blocked right-looking factorization** running entirely on the GPU (NB = 64 panel width):\n\n1. **`potf2Kernel`** — factorizes the 64×64 diagonal block inside shared memory (single block, column loop with rank‑1 updates).\n2. **`trsmKernel`** — `L21 = A21 · L11⁻ᵀ` for all rows below the panel; one thread per row, row tile staged in shared memory in column-major order so all global traffic is coalesced, 4-way partial sums to break the FP64 dependency chain.\n3. **`syrkUpdateKernel`** — trailing update `A22 -= L21·L21ᵀ`: 64×64 output tile per block, 16×16 threads with 4×4 register accumulators and a 16-deep shared-memory k-stage. Only lower-triangular tiles are computed, so the flop count matches the n³/3 of the original.\n4. **`zeroUpperKernel`** — the upper-triangle zeroing.\n\nAdditional work:\n- **Look-ahead schedule**: two streams + events factorize panel *k+1* concurrently with the bulk of panel *k*'s trailing update, so the serial POTF2/TRSM phases (~8% of GPU time) are hidden behind the SYRK.\n- Matrix generation (`B·Bᵀ`) and validation (`L·Lᵀ` + error reduction) also run on the GPU via `symProductKernel`/`errorReduceKernel`, computing the lower triangle and mirroring (bitwise identical, since the dot products are symmetric). The `rand_r` sequence stays sequential on the host, so the generated matrix is unchanged.\n- A small cached device-buffer pool avoids `cudaMalloc`/`cudaFree` (which synchronize) in the timed region; the CUDA context is created in `main` before timing. Host memory is deliberately *not* pinned — `cudaHostRegister` costs 25–55 ms per 128 MB here and buys no extra bandwidth (the link tops out at ~12.5 GB/s either way).\n\n`CMakeLists.txt` enables the CUDA language, compiles `cholesky.cpp` with nvcc via `LANGUAGE CUDA`, targets `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native`, and keeps the original host flags (`-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra`) through `-Xcompiler`. No new dependencies.\n\n## Results (RTX 3090, timed region includes H2D+D2H)\n\n| n | original | CUDA | speedup |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 4096 | 17792 ms | **71 ms** (323 GFLOPS) | 250× |\n| 8192 | — | **404 ms** (454 GFLOPS) | — |\n\nWhole-program time at n=4096 with validation: 123 s → 3.3 s.\n\nThe compute kernels run at ~620 GFLOPS of sustained FP64, which is the hardware ceiling for this card (82 SMs × 2 FP64 lanes at boost clock); the residual 20% of the measured time is the unavoidable PCIe transfer of the matrix in and out.\n\nCorrectness: validation passes for n = 1, 2, 63, 64, 65, 100, 129, 511, 512, 513, 1000, 1024, 2048, 4096 (max relative error ~1e-11 or better). Sum/min/max/samples from `-r` match a rebuilt copy of the original sequential program to 15–16 significant digits at n = 100/513/1024; only last-bit differences remain, since blocked factorization reorders the summations (the result hash therefore differs, as it does for any reassociation)."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":329,"cache_read_input_tokens":113844,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":329},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"06676667-9965-4a9b-86f2-d2b1d5470f9c","uuid":"32cf75ce-a5ac-45ca-95bb-7a2d0859e087","timestamp":"2026-09-13T16:46:01.509Z","request_id":"req_011Cf1n1rEYLKXg2m2oCdyss"}
